purpose: The native-<select> edge matrix that fixture 07 does not cover: an empty enumeration, a single answer, a selection near the END of a long list, duplicate labels, an over-long label, disabled options, and a disabled control. These are the shapes at which a clipping or read-back bug hides.
targeted_defect: Regression guard for the unified option ceiling (BUG-CATALOG-TRUNCATION-60). Fixture 07 pins the ceiling at scale; this one pins the BOUNDARIES and the read-back. A `value_committed` that degraded to the first option, a de-duplicated answer set, or a silently dropped disabled option would each pass fixture 07 untouched.

expect_controls.why: An enumeration with no answers is still a question. It must be captured, not dropped.
THE read-back assertion: the committed value is the 60th option, so a read that degraded to the first option would report opt001 and every generated verification would assert the wrong answer.
Three answers render identical text. De-duplicating them would report a 4-answer question as a 2-answer one.

options.first: Coverage tier extremely-long-descriptive-suffix extremely-long-descriptive-suffix extremely-long-descriptive-suffix extremely-long-descriptive-suffix extremely-long-descriptive-suffix extremely-long-d

expect_controls.why: A 422-char label clipped deterministically to MAX_OPTION (200) from the FRONT - a truncated label is still identifiable, an arbitrary slice is not.
A disabled OPTION is still an answer the question lists; dropping it would under-report the enumeration. The disabled state of the CONTROL is a separate signal.
The control is disabled; its enumeration is still captured honestly.
